title: Acute respiratory deterioration
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Check the prescribed target and the delivery device when a patient's breathing worsens.
Escalate according to the early warning score and local policy.
Record the response and keep monitoring.
Recognise that concern justifies review whatever the score.

sources.use: NEWS2 report: oxygen documentation, response tiers, record the response, concern overrides score
AARC oxygen therapy CPG: titrate within order
FDA public indexed limitations of pulse oximetry, including perfusion and skin pigmentation.
BTS 2017 selected emergency oxygen recommendations and 2019 target-range decision; not full appraisal
ATS 2026 adult noninvasive respiratory support recommendations, indexed primary text

required_sources: Full appraisal of respiratory deterioration and BTS oxygen guideline recommendations, including disease-specific pathways
Unit escalation policy and critical care outreach criteria
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.
Selected BTS oxygen and ATS 2026 respiratory support recommendations now supplement escalation teaching; diagnosis-specific treatment and complete appraisal remain outstanding.
No saturation target is stated; the target is the prescribed one.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
setting: A fictional adult receiving oxygen on a fictional unit.

steps.info: An adult receiving oxygen through a prescribed mask becomes visibly more breathless during observations. Saturation is drifting down, respiratory effort is increasing and the early-warning score is rising. The cause is not yet known.
steps.prompt: Which action addresses respiratory deterioration without treating the saturation display alone?

options.text: Stay with the patient, assess airway, breathing and circulation; call for help and provide authorised emergency support. Check device, target and observations in parallel.
options.feedback: A falling saturation and increasing breathing effort require immediate patient assessment. Use the early warning score and oxygen targets to inform the response, not as a reason to postpone emergency oxygen or ventilation support when indicated. Pulse oximetry estimates oxygenation, not ventilation; perfusion and skin pigmentation can affect accuracy. If the clinical picture and reading disagree, request further assessment and an appropriate alternative measurement without postponing emergency care. Request urgent blood gas assessment when hypercapnia is suspected, especially with new drowsiness or rising work of breathing. Emergency support for critical illness should not be withheld because of possible carbon dioxide retention; the team then individualizes oxygen and ventilation using blood gases and clinical response.
options.consequence: Patient-first assessment may identify a delivery problem or worsening respiratory failure while urgent clinical support is arranged.

options.text: Adjust the oxygen to maximum to restore the displayed saturation, record the new flow and repeat the oximeter measurement before assessing breathing or activating the emergency pathway.
options.feedback: Do not treat the display alone. Provide emergency oxygen or respiratory support promptly under the authorized pathway; after immediate stabilization, titrate according to the patient-specific plan.
options.consequence: A better displayed saturation could mask inadequate ventilation or persistent respiratory distress.

options.text: Maintain the current oxygen prescription because the saturation is still close to target, record the rising early-warning score and reassess the patient at the next scheduled observation.
options.feedback: Leaving deterioration unaddressed is unsafe even when saturation is near its target. Worsening effort or clinical concern warrants assessment and escalation.
options.consequence: Waiting for a clearer numerical change could allow respiratory failure to progress.

steps.info: At the next shared checkpoint, saturation has fallen further despite oxygen, breathing is laboured and the patient is slower to respond. The score is in the urgent-review range; clinical severity may require an emergency response.
steps.prompt: Which response is appropriate when effort and alertness worsen despite oxygen support?

options.text: Stay with the patient; urgently reassess and escalate, activating the emergency response if breathing is inadequate or instability is present. Arrange authorised respiratory support.
options.feedback: Clinical severity can require a higher response than the aggregate early warning score indicates. Do not wait for another score or routine review if the patient is unstable. ATS 2026 distinguishes acute hypoxemic failure, where high-flow nasal oxygen is recommended, from acute hypercapnic failure, where noninvasive ventilation is recommended. Suitability depends on the individual and the cause. If noninvasive support is being used, report worsening effort, consciousness, gas exchange or circulation promptly; do not allow a trial of support to delay indicated intubation.
options.consequence: Escalation and repeat assessment may identify a need for additional respiratory support before exhaustion progresses.

options.text: Obtain another complete set of observations and calculate the new score, documenting any change in alertness before requesting urgent review or starting additional respiratory support.
options.feedback: The trigger for urgent review has already been reached.
options.consequence: Waiting for another observation set could delay assessment of respiratory failure.

options.text: Review the available higher-dependency beds and independently arrange a transfer, postponing bedside emergency assessment until the receiving team can reassess the patient's breathing.
options.feedback: The reviewing clinician decides on escalation of care and transfer.
options.consequence: An uncoordinated transfer could interrupt monitoring or respiratory support and delay stabilization.

steps.info: At the final shared checkpoint, the clinician has changed the support plan. Saturation has improved and the score is lower, but the patient remains drowsier than baseline. Ventilation and clinical response need reassessment.
steps.prompt: How should the nurse respond to improved saturation with persistent altered alertness?

options.text: Record the response, reassess breathing and alertness, follow the monitoring plan and seek urgent further review despite the lower score.
options.feedback: NEWS2 asks for the response to be recorded and says any concern about the patient should prompt an urgent review whatever the score. Improved oxygenation does not establish adequate ventilation or explain ongoing drowsiness. Reassess airway, breathing and circulation, communicate the persistent change and request urgent further review; coordinate blood gas assessment as indicated without delaying emergency support.
options.consequence: Reassessment and handover may identify unresolved ventilatory failure or another cause of drowsiness despite improved saturation.

options.text: Document the new saturation and lower score and discontinue escalation, treating the improved oxygenation as sufficient evidence that the patient's persistent drowsiness has resolved.
options.feedback: The score is an aid to judgement; concern or a worsening trend justifies a further call.
options.consequence: Stopping escalation based on a better score could delay recognition of ongoing respiratory compromise.

options.text: Return to routine observation intervals and leave the previous clinical review undocumented, since the support has been changed and the score has fallen.
options.feedback: The response is recorded so that the next shift can see what was done.
options.consequence: Routine checks without documenting the plan could leave deterioration or treatment changes unrecognized.

learning_points: Assess the patient and provide authorised emergency support first; verify oxygen delivery and the prescribed target in parallel.
The early warning score triggers a response; escalate with an SBAR per local policy.
Record the response, monitor as directed, and call again whenever you remain concerned.
An acceptable oxygen saturation does not exclude inadequate ventilation; interpret oximetry in clinical context and escalate discordant findings.
Recognize deterioration despite oxygen or noninvasive support and escalate promptly for blood gases and respiratory-team assessment.
